# Results

The coefficient on board independence may possibly suggest that independent directors could
potentially reduce earnings management to some extent. It seems that this effect might arguably be
stronger in firms with dispersed ownership, although this could perhaps reflect other factors.

Our sample covers 4,112 firm-years from 2004 to 2019 (Table 1). Independent boards appear to be
somewhat more likely to replace the auditor after a restatement, which may potentially indicate
heightened monitoring.
